name: MI-05
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -13 point partisan lean
Incumbent Tim Walberg running with a large financial advantage
Democrat raised only about $56K with no outside spending or polls
Prediction markets price Walberg around 94% to win
model.rationale: The district's -13 point Republican lean, Walberg's incumbency and roughly $1M cash advantage, and a Democratic challenger who raised under $60K all point to a comfortable Republican hold, with markets agreeing at about 94% for Walberg.
model.watch: A sudden influx of outside spending or polling showing the challenger competitive would be the only realistic path to moving this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Walberg seeks another term in a southern Michigan district that leans Republican by about 13 points. He is a well-established incumbent with nearly a million dollars on hand, while Democratic challenger Christian Vukasovich has raised only about $56,000 and has no outside support. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but show no signs of serious campaigns.

No public polls or expert ratings exist for this race, but prediction markets give Walberg roughly a 94 percent chance of winning. With no evidence of a competitive dynamic, the forecast treats this as a safe Republican seat, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
